messages:
tara: noticing weird "ghost" allocations in eu-west1 warmpool - nodes show alloc=true but kubelet NotReady, scheduler still thinks capacity exists, leading to tiny-gpu pods pending and lots of tiny preempts. anyone else seeing this?
edo: yep. noticed about 15 tiny pods stuck pending and 3 larger jobs failing placement. I pulled the node list: some nodes have last-lease-refresh ~2m ago but kubelet heartbeat 10m ago.
tara: gross. paste: ```NODE gp-wrack-12 alloc=true lease_ts=2024-04-22T10:05:12Z kubelet_ts=2024-04-22T09:55:01Z Ready=False```
deploy-bot: autoscaler: warmpool-eu-west scaled up +4 (reason: pending pods > 20) at 10:08 UTC :rotating_light:
oliver: autoscaler reacted to scheduler false positives. cost note: that kind of spin-up for 12min = ~1.8k. we should avoid oscillation.
edo: root cause candidate: lease-controller and node-proxy heartbeats out of sync. lease-controller marks node allocated while node-proxy hasn't reported ready, scheduler predicates consider lease_allocated falsey and try to binpack, causing churn when kubelet isn't ready and pods get preempted.
tara: quick mitigation: set warmpool.eviction_tolerance=30s and warmpool.min=0 for eu-west for 15m to force reconcilation. doing it now.
sre-oncall: alert rule fired: preempt_rate=7/min; setting pager to watch. I'll mute non-critical autoscaler alerts during mitigation window.
oliver: we should also add a scheduler filter: if lease_ts older than kubelet_ts or kubelet NotReady, mark unschedulable. that will stop scheduler from assuming capacity. drafting a small admission filter.
edo: alternative: surface lease health as a separate resource and make autoscaler consult it before scale decisions. autoscaler can wait if many nodes in "allocating" but kubelet not ready.
tara: implemented a short-lived hotfix: lease-controller now treats 504/5xx as transient and leaves alloc=false until it can confirm node health. rolled to eu-west0 (canary).
deploy-bot: deployment lease-controller-canary v1.2.1 -> eu-west0 started at 10:12 UTC
oliver: pushed PR#510 with scheduler filter + unit tests, but want to run canary in staging first. can we gate release behind a metric: scheduler_false_capacity_rate?
sre-oncall: yes - add metric. I'll watch false_capacity_rate and preempt_count. current false_capacity_rate ~0.9% baseline, spiking to 8% during incident.
edo: long-term: consider making warmpool lifecycle transitions hold until kubelet ready + node-exporter heartbeats. Also add a short "grace window" where allocation is provisional and not counted by binpacker.
tara: agreed. added runbook step: if lease-controller upstream has >1% errors, toggle warmpool.min->0 and reconcile nodes. doc path: runbooks/warmpools.md line 87.
oliver: small note: tiny-gpu eviction churn seems worse when many tiny pods have podAntiAffinity == null. maybe adding soft-affinity for tiny workloads will let binpacker co-locate them and reduce fragmentation.
sre-oncall: metrics update: after canary and toggles, preempt_rate down to 1/min, false_capacity_rate 0.4%. continuing to monitor for 20m. :thumbsup:
tara: thanks everyone. follow-ups: 1) PR#510 scheduler filter canary (oliver) 2) autoscaler consult lease-health (edo) 3) warmpool lifecycle reconciliation doc (tara) 4) affinity suggestion trial for tiny-gpu (platform). closing when stable for 30m.
